thread:
maya: Customer hit our API from ECS tasks via PrivateLink. Intermittent 502 / connection reset. Happens after they enabled interface endpoint + private DNS. No changes to app code.

maya: original error from client: 
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/infer
* Connected to 10.10.5.12 (10.10.5.12) port 443
* ALPN, offering h2
* TLSv1.3 (INTERNAL), TLS alert, received fatal: unknown CA
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) SSL connect error
```

alex: ok can you paste traceroute / dig output from one of affected tasks? also what mode are ECS tasks (awsvpc/bridge)?

maya: awsvpc. dig +short api.redwood.example.com -> 10.10.5.12 (private endpoint ENI). aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces on ENI shows SG sg-0a1b2c allowing 443 from the client subnet.

jordan: two quick guesses: 1) TLS SNI/host mismatch (client resolves to vpce IP but SNI/Host header preserved?). 2) There's an inline TLS-inspecting proxy replacing certs.

nisha: also check if Private DNS mapping is enabled for the endpoint. If not, DNS might resolve external IP sometimes -> egress path and certs will match but traffic might be blocked by egress allowlist. If enabled, ensure the endpoint's private DNS is resolving to the endpoint in all AZs.

maya: digs from different AZs:
```
us-east-1a> dig +short api.redwood.example.com @10.0.2.2
10.10.5.12
us-east-1b> dig +short api.redwood.example.com @10.0.3.2
13.249.45.1
```

maya: so one AZ resolving to external public IP (13.249...) and one to VPCE IP. That explains intermittent.

alex: aha split-horizon DNS inconsistency. Could be Route53 resolver rules or conditional forwarder caching in their DNS forwarder. Are they using a custom DHCP option set or Route53 inbound endpoints?

maya: they have a Route53 resolver inbound in the VPC and a custom DNS forwarder (BIND) in a NAT'd subnet. The resolver rules point the domain to the endpoint, but the forwarder cache TTL is 300s.

jordan: two remediation paths: 1) ensure Private DNS is enabled on the interface endpoint so the AWS provided VPC DNS handles resolution consistently OR 2) update the customer's forwarder to forward queries for api.redwood.example.com to the VPC resolver endpoints (no caching).

nisha: also verify the client's TLS SNI actually contains api.redwood.example.com. If the app is setting Host header to the endpoint DNS name (vpce-...) but SNI is api.redwood..., passive proxies can still break. Run openssl s_client -connect 10.10.5.12:443 -servername api.redwood.example.com and check cert CN/SAN.

maya: ran openssl:
```
openssl s_client -connect 10.10.5.12:443 -servername api.redwood.example.com
# handshake completes, certificate presented for CN=api.redwood.example.com
```

maya: but when we curl from app container we see TLS unknown CA. Customer says they have a corporate TLS-mitm proxy on egress for some tasks.

alex: that matches. When traffic takes the public route via proxy, proxy replaces cert with corporate CA -> client rejects if corporate CA not trusted. When traffic hits VPCE directly, cert is fine. So inconsistent DNS -> intermittent.

nisha: suggested repro steps for customer: 
1) from an affected task/container, run:
```
# force lookup to endpoint IP
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.example.com:443:10.10.5.12 https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/health
```
2) from same task, force public IP to simulate broken path:
```
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.example.com:443:13.249.45.1 https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/health
```
Compare TLS certs and responses.

maya: customer ran these. Endpoint IP -> 200 OK, cert CN matches. Public IP -> connection succeeds but cert shows corporate CA (mitm) and client fails on verify.

jordan: next steps we recommended to customer:
- Fix DNS so all AZs consistently resolve to VPCE IPs (enable Private DNS or reconfigure forwarder rules).
- Whitelist Redwood if they must use proxy egress, and install corporate CA in their containers/trust store (not ideal).
- Ensure ENI SGs allow inbound from all client subnets, and check NACLs for asymmetric rules.

maya: customer will roll out DNS forwarder change and test. I'll update thread once they confirm. :white_check_mark:
